mike_customer: Hi team — after the 03:00 deploy our API calls to /v1/generate started returning 403. Happening from our prod host only. Example request id from response: req_20240327_9f3b2c. Can you check?

elaine_support: Sorry you're hitting this, thanks for the heads up. Can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces + the exact response body (include request id)? Also include the x-org-id and x-project-id you used.

mike_customer: Here's the exact curl I ran from our app host (sanitized token):

```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-org-id: org-78a2" \
  -H "x-project-id: proj-33b" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"hello"}'
```

Response (HTTP/1.1 403):
```json
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "message": "organization scope mismatch",
  "request_id": "req_20240327_9f3b2c"
}
```

sam_engineer: thanks — that req id matches an ingress hit on our edge. Quick hypothesis: the service key you used is scoped to org-5c9, not org-78a2 (we see a scope mismatch in the auth booth). Two quick repros to try: 1) run the same curl but with the org header that matches the key (org-5c9) and 2) drop x-project-id entirely (some older tokens are org-scoped and proxies can treat project header as override).

elaine_support: Also, can you run with `curl -v --trace-ascii trace.txt ...` and attach trace.txt so we can check header canonicalization? And please include the full response headers (we want the X-Redwood-Request-Id the edge returns).

mike_customer: ran test 1 (swapped org header) — now getting 401. New resp: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized. Body:
```json
{
  "error":"unauthorized",
  "message":"invalid token scope",
  "request_id":"req_20240327_af12d4"
}
```

sam_engineer: that lines up with a rotated key scenario. Can you paste the token prefix (first 8 chars) of the sk used? we can correlate with our keymap. If you prefer, give us the request ids + the trace.txt and we can look up the full auth log.

mike_customer: token prefix: sk_live_1a2b3c4d. trace.txt attached in the ticket (I uploaded to the portal). Also noticed our infra adds an internal header `x-internal-proxy: true` — could that be rewriting x-project-id?

elaine_support: good call — in the past some proxies canonicalize headers and strip custom ones. We'll check the ingress logs for header rewrite rules. Sam, can you grep the auth logs for that token prefix and the two request ids?

sam_engineer: on it. quick grep shows these patterns:
```
2024-03-27T03:02:18Z ingress[edge-2]: incoming req req_20240327_9f3b2c headers: x-org-id: org-78a2, x-project-id: proj-33b, authorization: sk_live_1a2b3c4d...
2024-03-27T03:02:19Z authsvc[auth-1]: token sk_live_1a2b3c4d scope: org-5c9 (revoked-for-org-78a2) -> deny 403
2024-03-27T03:07:02Z ingress[edge-2]: incoming req req_20240327_af12d4 headers: x-org-id: org-5c9, x-project-id: proj-33b, authorization: sk_live_1a2b3c4d...
2024-03-27T03:07:03Z authsvc[auth-1]: token sk_live_1a2b3c4d scope: org-5c9 (valid) -> but token flagged expired -> deny 401
```

sam_engineer: so two things: (A) token is tied to org-5c9 but the first request used org-78a2 which caused a scope mismatch -> 403. (B) the key appears to have been rotated/marked expired around 03:05 which explains the 401 on the second attempt. This is consistent with a rotation that happened around the deploy window.

mike_customer: ahh okay that makes sense. We see a key-rotation job kicked off in our infra exactly at 03:04. We accidentally rolled a consumer key out that was expired for the service.

elaine_support: thanks for digging. Next steps: we will 1) label these request ids on the internal ticket so infra can correlate, 2) create a debug bundle for the authsvc traces and ingress traces (sam will attach), and 3) recommend you use a short window fallback key in your deploy to avoid auth blips on rotation.

devops-bot: :spiral_note_pad: Created support ticket RDW-2024-3221 and attached initial logs.

mike_customer: thanks — I'll update our deploy to keep old key for 5 mins. Please add any mitigation notes.

elaine_support: will do. If you can upload a redwood-debug bundle (the portal link is in the ticket) with the trace.txt and the response bodies, we'll close the loop faster. Appreciate the quick repro steps and the trace file. :thumbsup:

sam_engineer: attaching a snippet we will put in the debug bundle for posterity:
```
Recommended repro steps for support:
1) run the original curl exactly as the customer did (preserve x-org-id + x-project-id)
2) if 403, swap x-org-id to the org the token maps to and try again
3) if 401 after rotation window, capture ingress trace and full authsvc logs referencing request_id
```

mike_customer: done — uploaded bundle and left RDW-2024-3221 in the portal. Closing on our side once we confirm the short-key fallback works.
